newsitem.title: UK: Gasoline buyers help oil prices in face of Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Gasoline buyers help oil prices in face of Iraq.

text.p: Oil prices skipped higher again on Tuesday sparked by a fresh run of gasoline buying in the United States while shrugging off concerns over an Iraqi export dash.
Benchmark North Sea Brent crude futures for September ended 27 cents higher in London at $18.84 a barrel.
Brent had slumped a dollar a barrel in a week as Iraqi exports loomed large under the second phase of its oil-for-food exchange with the United Nations.
But dealers on Tuesday turned their attention back to inventory holdings in the world's largest oil market, the United States.
Weekly U.S. statistics from the American Petroleum Institute (API), out later on Tuesday, were expected to show a fall in gasoline and crude oil stocks.
"People are anticipating a stockdraw when the APIs come out and that's helped turn the market around," said a dealer in London.
Traders kept a close eye on Iraqi developments, awaiting confirmation that a first shipment from the Turkish pipeline outlet of Ceyhan would set sail this week.

Iraq is targeting a post-Gulf War export record of some 1.5 million barrels a day (bpd) in an attempt to raise as much cash as possible by an interim deadline of September 5 for a billion dollars worth of oil sales.
The supertanker Arcadia was anchored at Ceyhan waiting for oil trader Bayoil to receive U.N. approval to load Iraq's first shipment since the end of May.
Iraq has already scheduled 17.5 million barrels, 875,000 bpd, from Ceyhan but is struggling to secure buyers from its Gulf port Mina al Bakr.
Paltry plans for al Bakr sailings suggest Baghdad could struggle to reach its ambitious end-August export target.
Japanese buyers are ruled out by Iraq for political reasons and Chinese firms have discounted reports they might lift large quantities.
